cells: Audits receipts and expenditure of the Central Government
Examines companies owned or funded by government
Checks that public money is spent legally and efficiently

blocks.content: The CAG is the guardian of the public purse and controls the entire financial system of the country at both the levels—the Centre and the state.

rows: Acts purely as an Auditor General; money can be withdrawn from the treasury without CAG consent.
Acts as both Comptroller and Auditor General; executive cannot withdraw money without CAG authorization.
Not a member of Parliament and does not attend parliamentary debates.
Is an official who acts directly as an officer of the House of Commons.
Ex-post audit (audits expenditure after money has already been spent).
Ex-ante and ex-post control (controls issue of public money prior to expenditure as well as post-audit).

items: CAG of India acts only as an Auditor General (ex-post audit) and not as a Comptroller, meaning executive authorities can draw money from the Consolidated Fund without CAG's prior approval.
Administrative expenses of the CAG office, including salaries, allowances, and pensions of persons serving in that office, are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India and are non-votable.
CAG is not eligible for further office either under the Government of India or under the Government of any State after ceasing to hold office.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The CAG derives authority and powers from Article 149 of the Constitution and the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971.
Audits all expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India, Consolidated Funds of States, and UTs having a Legislative Assembly.
Audits accounts related to the Contingency Fund of India and the Public Account of India, as well as state-level contingency funds and public accounts.
Submits three annual audit reports to the President (Appropriation Accounts, Finance Accounts, and Public Undertakings), who lays them before Parliament.
Functions as an agent of Parliament and acts as a guide, friend, and philosopher to the Public Accounts Committee (PAC).
